card.title: 4. FALLSCHIRMJÄGER
card.text: Deployment: Choose a unit in hand with a cost of 2 or less. Set its cost to 0.
card.flavorText: The 4th Fallschirmjäger Regiment was part of the 1st Fallschirmjäger-Division which was the German Luftwaffe's premier airborne unit during WWII. Under General Kurt Student, it executed the daring 1940 assault on Belgium's Fort Eben-Emael, using gliders to assault and neutralize the fortress. The division also participated in the Battle of Crete in 1941, suffering heavy losses that led Hitler to limit future large-scale airborne operations. After Crete, the division served on the Eastern Front near Leningrad and Stalino (named Donetsk today). In 1943, it was redeployed to Italy, engaging in battles at Ortona and Monte Cassino. Throughout the Italian Campaign, the division was noted for its tenacity, delaying Allied advances despite being outnumbered. In April 1945, it retreated across the Po River and surrendered in early May. The division's structure included three parachute regiments, an artillery regiment, and support units like anti-aircraft and engineer battalions. It was commanded by officers such as Richard Heidrich and Karl-Lothar Schulz. As the war neared its end, the division retreated across northern Italy and ultimately surrendered in May 1945.
